headline: US stocks closed lower as chip rebound faded and oil climbed on Middle East tensions ahead of major tech earnings
raw_text:
- Major US indices ended lower, with the Dow (DIA) logging a third straight decline as an early attempt to rebound from the recent slide stalled amid Middle East tensions and caution before Big Tech results.
- Chipmakers surrendered most of a strong intraday advance, leaving the PHLX Semiconductor Index only modestly higher after being up sharply earlier in the session.
- Apple (AAPL) fell more than 2%, pressuring the Dow (DIA) and contributing to an ongoing rotation out of mega-cap tech and growth names.
- Energy and defensive sectors showed relative resilience as Brent crude (@QA) rose to around $89 and WTI (@CL) also gained, with US-Iran exchanges briefly pushing oil above $90.
- IREN (IREN) jumped after saying about 85% of its raised 2026 AI Cloud ARR target over $4bn is under contract.
- CIFR (CIFR) and Archer Aviation (ACHR) were among notable intraday gainers, while volatile low-float names such as ZYBT (ZYBT), MF (MF) and ADVB (ADVB) recorded outsized moves on retail momentum trading and short-squeeze activity.
- PVLA (PVLA) and GVH (GVH) were among the session’s sharpest decliners, with GVH (GVH) and certain warrants dropping on company-specific announcements.
- Investors weighed questions about AI momentum and reports of hedge funds selling US tech at a record pace ahead of this week’s Big Tech earnings, including Tesla (TSLA).
- Broader macro and policy developments included Jamie Dimon warning markets underestimate risks and saying he would not buy stocks or Treasurys here, Trump proposing 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods, a judge pausing the proposed Paramount–Warner Bros. (WBD) merger, and Boeing (BA) winning a reprieve as 4th Circuit decertifies investor class in shareholder suit over Jan 2024 Alaska Airlines 737 Max 9 incident.
- After-hours, Cracker Barrel (CBRL) rose after selling Maple Street Biscuit Co., completing a $77M sale-leaseback and raising FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA outlook as mixed reactions to Q2 earnings and the upcoming Hasbro (HAS) report before Tuesday’s open, along with potential further Middle East developments, were set to guide near-term direction.
